what_it_states: Differentially private federated learning framework (UDP-FL): per-client gradient clipping and additive noise from a chosen mechanism (Gaussian, Laplace, Staircase), with a 'Harmonizer' that calibrates noise multipliers through Renyi-DP accounting (Algorithm 3), mode-connectivity aggregation (Algorithms 1-2), heterogeneous-budget penalty update, and shuffler amplification lemmas quoted from Girgis et al. Section 4: Table 3 Renyi divergences; Theorems 1/3 (Staircase RDP expression, Appendix A.1/A.4); a staircase density written with ||x||_1 level sets (Section 4.2) used as the mechanism definition; Lemma quoting Geng-Viswanath for the scalar minimum expected amplitude at nu = 1/(1+e^{lambda/2}); Theorem 4 expected l1 distance of output parameters under staircase noise; Theorems 5-6 mode-connectivity convergence statements under smoothness/strong-convexity assumptions; Appendix D Gaussian/Laplace RDP and l1-distance statements. Section 5 / Appendix E experiments (MNIST, Medical MNIST, CIFAR-10, UTKFace; membership, reconstruction and attribute-inference attacks). Introduction and Section 3.1 repeat the cited headline that the staircase mechanism is optimal for l1 and l2 metrics over a wide epsilon range (citing scalar Geng-Viswanath ISIT 2014 and R2DP).
what_it_does_not_state: No all-law optimality theorem of its own; the optimality headline is cited from the scalar staircase result, and the ||x||_1-level-set staircase formula is a mechanism definition with no stated optimality claim for vector or planar MSE; no l1-diamond sensitivity model with squared-Euclidean MSE; no selector between diamond and rounded cores; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2.
